# Build decisions

Decisions, engineering assumptions and unresolved business rules made while running `ADX_AUTONOMOUS_BUILD.md`. Numbered `BD-nn` so they don't collide with the `D-nn` decisions in `docs/architecture.md`. When one of these changes an architecture decision, the architecture doc gets a new `D-nn` entry too and the old one is marked replaced, never deleted.

Business policy is never invented here. Where a rule is missing it is listed under "Unresolved business rules" with who supplies it, and the code ships the rule as typed configuration in an unconfigured state.

## Decisions

### BD-01. Build ledger lives in `docs/build/`
2026-10-17. `progress.json` (task states and evidence), `decisions.md` (this file), `verification.md` (commands and results, fake-provider versus live) and `inventory.md` (baseline). Updated after each task and committed with it.

### BD-02. Commit per task, locally, one-line Conventional Commits
2026-10-17. The checkout has no remote. Each task that passes `make check` and `make test` is committed on `main` so progress is diffable. No force-push or reset.

### BD-03. The spec's "existing lead ingestion" and mock layer do not exist here
2026-10-17. The checkout is the pristine baseline. Lead import, analytics screens and mock selection are built new in phase 1 rather than extended. Recorded so nobody looks for code that was never there.

### BD-04. Toolchain installs
2026-10-17. pnpm 10.33.4, sqlc 1.31.1 and golangci-lint 2.14.0 were installed user-locally (see `inventory.md`). Nothing else was installed system-wide. air is optional and was skipped.

## Engineering assumptions

Defaults chosen so the platform can be built without the owner's policy. Each one can be overridden by configuration and none activates an external effect.

- EA-01. External mutation policy defaults to disabled for every provider and action until an admin configures it (spec section 2).
- EA-02. Assistant tools default to read-only.
- EA-03. Missing identity denies; missing workspace or account scope denies; missing business evidence is null or "needs review", never 0 or a guess.
- EA-04. An unresolved customer match is never auto-merged.

### BD-53. A client is a workspace: provider accounts and projects are unique within it, one provider account belongs to one client, sessions take their workspace from memberships, and industry configuration is versioned per client and can never grant permissions
2026-10-17. `accounts` and `projects` gain `workspace_id` (migration 00035 rebuilds both tables; existing rows belong to Reportage) with uniqueness on (workspace, type, external id) and (workspace, name), so two clients may both have Google Ads account "123" or a project called "The Wadi". Every read of accounts and projects filters by the actor's workspace; an account of another client is "not connected" to policy decisions, the kill switch, lead imports, token reads and launch dispatch, never "exists but forbidden". Connecting a provider account another workspace already holds is a conflict: a location or ad account belongs to one client, because sharing one would show each other's figures. The GoHighLevel webhook resolves its workspace from the event's `locationId` through the connected account, and accepts an event without one only while a single workspace exists. The daily refresh runs each account as ADX in that account's own workspace. Platform admins (admins of Reportage, workspace 1) provision clients; the creator becomes the first admin; workspace admins add existing ADX people with at most their own role and cannot remove the last enabled admin. A sign-in lands in Reportage when the person belongs to it, else their first workspace; switching ends the session and issues a new token, and the role is the membership's role in the new workspace. The dev admin switches through a cookie that only the dev actor reads. Industry configuration (industry, vocabulary, stages, qualifiers, notes) is a numbered version per workspace, never edited in place; Reportage's version 1 is seeded from the reference document, a new client starts with its own empty version 1; documents carrying `role`, `permissions`, `members` or workspace keys are refused at the edge before decoding, so configuration cannot widen what anyone may do.

- **Why.** The acceptance: the same provider ids and names across tenants never leak, Reportage's history keeps the definitions it was built under after another client's change, and cross-tenant rows are unreachable through any entry point.
- **Audit.** A scan of every query on a workspace-bearing table without a workspace filter (147 queries) found follow-up writes keyed by a row already read with its workspace, lease and tick queries for jobs, and three id lookups fed from requests: `GetProject`, `GetAccountByID` and `GetAccount`. The first now takes the workspace; the other two are checked by every caller. Jobs that run across clients (`ListAllAccounts`, `ListEnabledResearchSchedulesAllWorkspaces`, `ListDispatchableIntents`) carry each row's workspace into the actor they act as.
- **Cost.** The identity of a client is the workspace id on the session row; nothing in the request names it. The `claim` rule means an agency serving two clients from one ad account would have to connect it to one of them; that is the documented limitation until a case needs otherwise.

### BD-54. A connector's capabilities are a catalog in code with a reason for everything unsupported; ADX publishes nothing; messaging adapters exist for WhatsApp Cloud and SMTP but are wired only with live writes on, and native work surfaces stop at what the record needs
2026-10-17. `core/connections.Catalog` lists, per connector, every read, write and publish capability with supported, wired and a reason. Publish is never supported: a reviewed asset is handed to a person. Audience and conversion uploads, Meta lead forms and pixel, GoHighLevel conversations and pipeline writes, WhatsApp templates and inbound, SMS and mailbox reading are named as unsupported with the reason. `GET /api/connections/capabilities` merges the catalog with what `cmd/adx` configured, and the connections screen shows it beside the accounts. Two outreach adapters are added behind the existing `Messenger` seam: WhatsApp Business Cloud (plain text, inside Meta's 24-hour window; a refusal fails the draft with Meta's code and reason) and SMTP for the email channel (Message-ID derived from the draft's idempotency key). `outreach.Combine` routes by channel, first adapter wins a shared channel, and returns nil for none. Both are constructed only when `ADX_LIVE_WRITES=1`, and a send still needs the channel mode on, the person unsuppressed, quiet hours over and a person's approval. The daily refresh treats a failing account as that account's failure: an unknown provider is skipped, a revoked credential fails its own run, and the other accounts' runs complete. The native-versus-integrate review in `docs/build/native-review.md` records, per capability, user value, maintenance and the decision: records, tasks, a minimal board, review and schedules are native; lead capture, ad delivery, messaging, calling, research and identity are integrated; publishing, audience uploads and intelligence datasets are not built.

- **Why.** The pass conditions: a connector logo never implies unsupported publishing, a disconnected optional source does not break unrelated accounts, and native-versus-integrate decisions include maintenance and user value.
- **Cost.** The messaging policy is still unsupplied, so the adapters are code without a route to a customer: the live gate for B4.3 stays blocked on the policy, not on an adapter. WhatsApp template messages are not built, which means outreach to someone who has not written in 24 hours fails rather than sends.

### BD-55. One metered model for every consumer with a server-wide daily cap; a model release is approved only by a person, never on a regression, and the running model is reported against the approved one; load figures exist only with their conditions; backups prune by retention only after a new one succeeds
2026-10-17. `ops.Meter` wraps the one model client every domain uses (assistant, plans, research, call readings, workflow steps) and refuses every call once the server's UTC-day usage reaches `ADX_MODEL_DAILY_TOKEN_CAP` (default ten million tokens, 0 off), recording usage and refusals per day and model in `model_usage_days` so a restart does not reset the count. The per-workspace assistant budget and per-run workflow budgets stay as they were; `/api/ops/cost` reports all three against usage, with money only when a price is configured. A model release is a candidate evaluated by replaying every labelled qualification call's transcript through the candidate with the live reading prompt (`qualification.ReadTranscript`, extracted so both paths read identically); an unusable reading counts as a disagreement, a missing transcript is skipped and named, and no call is changed. Promotion is an admin's act, refused below the required labelled count, below the required agreement, or below the approved release's agreement (a regression), and never happens on its own; the approved release is a record, and `/ops` warns when `ADX_MODEL_NAME` is not it. `adx loadtest DURATION CONCURRENCY` runs a fixed mix (person create, person list, signal ingest, evidence record, 64 KB asset write) against a scratch database and records operations, errors, p50/p95/max and the host, CPU count, Go version, workers and mix; the ops view shows the latest measurement with those conditions or says none exists, and nothing in the product quotes throughput otherwise. `adx backup` prunes stamped directories older than `ADX_BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS` only after a new backup succeeded and never touches other directories; the default keeps everything until Reportage names a period.

- **Why.** The pass conditions: cost and runaway budgets enforce configured limits, a model regression prevents automatic promotion, recovery reproduces linked state, and no throughput claim without measured conditions.
- **Measured.** On the build machine (Apple M3 Pro, 11 CPUs, go1.27.2, SQLite in WAL mode on the local SSD, 8 workers, 10 s): 21,163 operations, 2,115 operations per second, p50 1.0 ms, p95 15.2 ms, max 70.7 ms, 0 errors. This is a developer laptop against a scratch database, not the production host; the runbook says to measure there before quoting anything.
- **Cost.** The cap is server-wide, not per workspace, because the model client has no workspace; a noisy client can exhaust the day for the others, and the cost view shows who spent what so an admin can see it. Storage was not changed: SQLite handled the measured mix with sub-millisecond medians, and nothing measured calls for more.

### BD-62. Landing pages get a richer template and Adx drafts into it
2026-10-19. The page document grew the sections a property launch page needs: a hero (one studio picture with a line over it), stats (figures with labels), a gallery (studio pictures), a payment plan (rows of share and milestone), a location (address and a map link), and a twin slug that links the page to the same page in the other language. Pictures are the studio's files by SHA-256, served public at `/api/files/{sha}`, so renders and the pictures Adx made are what pages are built from; the engine's asset images stay available as the `image` section. Readiness scans stats and plan cells as claims, so a figure in a box is checked against approved facts like a figure in a sentence. Then `POST /api/pages/draft` asks the model for a page: given the brand's approved facts, pending facts it must not state, the offer when one is named, and the project's picture ids, it answers through a tool with the sections, and the draft is constrained before saving: stats and plan rows no fact or offer states are dropped and noted, picture ids not given are dropped, an offer section with no offer goes, a form is ensured at the end. With no language it drafts English and Arabic as twins; with a page id it drafts a new version of that page. The result is always a draft a person reviews and publishes; readiness still gates launch.

- **Why.** The flow Hisham chose: Adx drafts, a person approves, and the template first, so what Adx writes into has a hero and a plan rather than paragraphs only.
- **Cost.** The engine's page editor doesn't edit the new sections yet; a drafted hero, stats or plan is edited by drafting again with instructions or by the JSON. Arabic is the model's and is marked for review by the readiness warnings as before.

### BD-61. Studio makes content: Adx writes concepts from approved facts and pictures them with Google's image model; video and page drafting follow
2026-10-19. Nothing in either build generated content until now; the studio laid out copy a person typed over renders a person uploaded. Now a Creatives project can ask Adx for concepts (`POST /api/creative/projects/{id}/concepts/generate`): the model is given the brand's approved facts, pending facts it must not state, current offers and the concepts the project already has, and must answer through a tool with English and Arabic blocks in the studio's shape, the ad platform's text fields, and an imagery prompt. Any stat whose figure no approved fact or offer states is dropped and named in a note; a concept with no title in either language is not saved; codes collide with nothing. Then a concept can be pictured (`POST /api/creative/concepts/{id}/imagery`): the imagery prompt plus a fixed style line (photoreal property marketing, no text or logos in the picture, a calm area for a headline) goes to Google's image model (`providers/google`, Gemini API, `gemini-3.1-flash-image` by default, `ADX_GEMINI_API_KEY` and `ADX_IMAGE_MODEL`), optionally with the project's renders as references, and each picture comes back as a render of the project labelled with the concept's code, so the generator and the editor lay copy over it like any uploaded render. Text is never asked of the image model: Arabic and English are composed by the studio, where the letterforms are right and the words stay editable. The decisions taken with Hisham: static ads may use AI imagery freely; video ads will be both motion-from-renders and AI-generated, the person picking per concept; landing pages get a richer template first and then Adx drafts into it for a person to approve.

Video ads followed the same day (`POST /api/creative/concepts/{id}/video`): a video ad is a studio ad of kind `video` in 9:16, named `<concept>_<name>_VIDEO_<lang>_9x16.mp4`, with an MP4 as each version's file and a poster JPEG as its preview, reviewed on the board like any ad. It is made by a run (`studio_video`, worked by the jobs worker): motion moves up to four of the project's pictures with a slow zoom and dissolves and holds the finished story ad in that language at the end (`providers/ffmpeg`, the ffmpeg binary on the path or `ADX_FFMPEG`); or Veo grows an eight-second clip from the first picture and the concept's imagery prompt (`providers/google`, `predictLongRunning` polled until done, `ADX_VIDEO_MODEL` overriding `veo-3.1-generate-preview`), with a poster taken by ffmpeg. The person picks motion or the model per ask; the same ask twice while it runs returns the running run.

- **Why.** The brand-to-live-campaign loop had a hole where the creative work is: everything downstream (review, readiness, launch) existed, and the first step was a person with Photoshop.
- **Cost.** One more key and bill. Generated pictures are kept as renders, so a project's render list grows with every ask; hiding a render keeps ads already built on it. The model's Arabic is written by a language model and marked as needing native review, as before.

### BD-60. Create is called Studio
2026-10-19. The first door is Studio: the sidebar, the door filters on Home, Inbox and Present, and the paths (`/studio/...`, with `/create/...` redirecting). The internal door key is `studio` too, so nothing says Create any more.

- **Why.** Studio says what the door is for: the brand's research, plans, creatives, pages and launch are made there. Create read as a verb with no object.
- **Cost.** Old links keep working through the redirect; bookmarks and docs that say Create are simply out of date.

### BD-59. Creative Studio is ported as core/studio beside core/creative; the designed Creatives screens run on it
2026-10-19. The designed Creatives screens (`/creative`, `/creative/$projectId`, upload, concept, editor and the public review board at `/review/$key`) call `/api/creative/...`, `/api/files/...` and `/api/review/...`, which the old server had and the engine did not. Those endpoints and their domain are ported as `core/studio`: concepts and ads in four sizes, uploaded pictures and editor publishes as immutable versions, decisions and pinned comments bound to a version, renders and render picks, brand kit JSON, the review link. Files are stored once by SHA-256 under `ADX_FILES_DIR` (`store/blobs`), served public at `/api/files/{sha}` because the board shows them to people without accounts, and copied by `adx backup`. The engine's `core/creative` (brief to layout to render to approval, on `assets.Store`) stays as it is. The two overlap on what a version and an approval are and will be reconciled once one has carried real work; the studio's tables are `creative_projects`, `creative_concepts`, `creative_ads`, `creative_ad_versions`, `creative_decisions`, `creative_comments`, `creative_renders`, `creative_render_picks` and `files`, which don't collide with the engine's `creatives` and `creative_versions`. Type names were made unique for the TypeScript generator (`AdVersion`, `AdDraft`, `BoardDecision`), and `json.RawMessage` now generates as `unknown` rather than `string`, since the wire carries the parsed object; two engine screens that assumed a string were corrected.

- **Why.** The Inbox's Wadi launch card and the Creatives screens lost their pictures when the designed app moved onto the engine, because the ads lived behind endpoints only the old server had. Porting the domain whole keeps the screens' behaviour and their tests; mapping it onto `core/creative`'s lifecycle would have been a redesign of both.
- **Trying it.** `ADX_ENV=dev adx seed-demo` fills an empty dev database with Reportage and The Wadi: six approved facts, an approved launch offer, a creative project with two placeholder renders and a concept with copy in both languages and an imagery prompt, so every Studio action has something to work on. It does nothing when Reportage exists.
- **Moving data.** `adx import-studio <old-data-dir>` copies an old server's Creative Studio data (its `adx.db` and `files/`) into this server: projects matched by name in the default workspace, then concepts, ads, versions, renders, reviews, comments and picks, with every file put in `ADX_FILES_DIR`. A project that already has creatives is skipped, so a second run adds nothing. Who did what is not carried, since the old user ids mean nothing here.
- **Cost.** Two creative models in one server until they are reconciled, and two file stores (`ADX_ASSETS_DIR` for the engine's renders, `ADX_FILES_DIR` for the studio's uploads). The studio's reads are scoped to the actor's workspace at the project lists only; the per-id routes trust the project the id belongs to, which is fine with one workspace and must change before a second.

### BD-58. Brands and Start a brand run on the engine; Brand knowledge is the brand page
2026-10-18. The first designed screens rewired to the engine's API: Brands (`/brands`, from `/api/brands`), the brand page (`/brands/$brandId`, from `/api/brands/{id}` with facts, conflicts, offers, projects and the brand's research briefs) and Start a brand (`/brands/new`). Start creates the brand (`kind: own`, the brief and results as notes), its first project, assigns it, creates a research brief from the website, pages and competitors given, and starts the run. The specialists chosen and the skills and template file names are kept in the brand's notes until the registry (B5.2) has a place for them. Brand knowledge's own screen is gone: it was the brand page with sample data. Research (`/studio/research`) followed the same day: a brief's items, competitor resolution, pages read, keyword ideas and the audit from `/api/research/briefs/{id}`; schedules, market events and comparative reports stay on the engine's screen until brought over. Media plans (`/studio/plans`) too: list, versions, validation, allocations, assumptions, requirements, accept and draft-from-research from `/api/plans`; creating the plan frame and manual version edits stay on the engine's screen. Landing pages (`/studio/pages`) likewise: list, preview, deployments, readiness, test submissions and form submissions from `/api/pages`, with `/api/pages` now returning each page's brand, latest and published versions; editing a page's document stays on the engine's screen. Launch (`/studio/launch`) reads `/api/measurement/readiness`, `/api/executions/launch` and `/api/executions/milestones`; authorizing stays on the engine's screen.

- **Why.** These are the screens the CEO's flow starts on, and the engine already had everything they show. Nothing on them is sample any more.
- **Cost.** The old project hub (`/brands/$projectId`, analytics and leads per development on sample data) is removed rather than ported; the per-project figures return when Analytics is rewired to `/api/analytics`.

### BD-57. The designed web app and the engine build are merged: engine server, designed shell, engine screens kept under /engine until each designed screen is rewired
2026-10-18. Two builds grew from the same baseline: this engine (server, plain screens, ledger) and a designed web app (ink-on-paper design language, Home desk, Inbox, Present, Start a brand, Create steps on sample data, a Creative Studio port with its own Go domain). The engine is the base from here. The designed `web/src` replaces the engine's, and the engine's screens and API clients move to `web/src/engine/`, reachable from the sidebar's Engine item at `/engine/...`, so every real capability keeps a working UI. A designed screen that still runs on sample data carries a Sample chip and types from `web/src/api/types.legacy.ts` (the old server's generated types, hand-kept, never regenerated); rewiring it means switching to `@/api/types.gen` and the engine's endpoints, then deleting its engine twin. The engine's naming stands: a Brand is Reportage or a competitor and a development such as The Wadi is a Project under it; the designed app's "brand = development" wording is reverted as screens are rewired.

- **Why.** The engine has the behaviour and the tests; the designed app has the experience the CEO walked through. Keeping both reachable means nothing shipped is lost while the join happens screen by screen, and nothing on sample data can pass for connected.
- **Not carried over yet.** The designed app's Creative Studio (canvas editor, uploads, review board with comments) depends on its own Go domain (`core/creative`, migration 00007 in the old tree) that this server doesn't have; its screens are parked unlinked under `/creative` and the sidebar's Creatives points at the engine's creatives screen. Porting that domain onto this server's asset and approval lifecycle (B3.1) is the next Go task. Its GoHighLevel lead screens and stage table are likewise mock-only until rewired to `/api/leads` and the funnel settings.
- **Cost.** Two sets of UI for a while, and two API client layers (`web/src/api/client.ts` with mock gating, `web/src/engine/api/client.ts` straight to the server). Both go as the rewiring completes.

### BD-56. The build ends with one cross-phase journey test, a generated capability matrix that separates local proof from live need, task statuses reconciled to the ledger, and zero production verification claimed
2026-10-17. `server/journey/journey_test.go` runs brand, project, typed plan and accepted version, reviewed and approved 1:1 creative, published page, form submission to counted event, person, derived and scored signal, opportunity, learning record with an outcome attached to the adopted intervention, then provisions a second client with the same project name and proves it sees none of it. `docs/build/capability-matrix.md` is generated from `progress.json` and the task titles, lists every task's local state and exact live blocker, the connector matrix in short, and the inputs live use needs with who supplies them. `tasks.json` statuses now mirror `progress.json`; a reconciliation of every recorded path and test package against the tree found one stale path (a config file that lives in `main.go`), corrected. Every task is `implemented_local`; none is `verified`, because no provider account, model key, telecom route, messaging policy or hosting approval was supplied to this build, and the ledger says so per task rather than rounding up.

- **Why.** The pass conditions: all task evidence reconciles to code and tests, no blocked task is mislabelled verified, lacking credentials and approvals are listed with local evidence, and the checks pass.
- **Not done.** Operator-effort review with real business users (nobody was available to this build); browser inspection of the newer screens (the web app typechecks and lints, and the API behind each screen is tested, but no browser journey ran); live anything.

## Unresolved business rules

Supplied by Abdul (Reportage CEO, owner of this build) or by whoever he names. Dependent behaviour stays disabled or unconfigured until then.

| Rule | Needed by | State |
|---|---|---|
| Final GoHighLevel status-to-stage mapping | B1.2, B1.3 | unconfigured |
| MQL/SQL criteria | B4.2 | unconfigured |
| Attribution-conflict resolution (Google and Meta both claim a lead) | B1.3 | unconfigured; claims kept separate |
| Source precedence for price/inventory facts | B2.1 | unconfigured; conflicts need review |
| Approved budgets and write privileges per account | B0.4, B3.4 | unconfigured; writes disabled |
| Urgent anomaly thresholds | B1.4 | unconfigured; checks don't fire |
| Calling, recording and contact policy | B4.4, B4.5 | unconfigured; live calling disabled |
| Retention periods | B0.5, B6.3 | unconfigured; nothing deleted automatically |
| Reporting recipients | B1.4 | unconfigured; nothing delivered |
| Exact Excel media-plan template and marketing skill file | B2.3 | missing; exact-template adapter blocked |

### BD-05. Production never creates its storage directories
2026-10-17. `checkStorage` in `cmd/adx` requires the directories of `ADX_DB_PATH` and `ADX_ASSETS_DIR` to exist outside dev. Dev creates them.

- **Why.** A missing directory on a server means the volume isn't mounted. Creating it would start a fresh, empty ADX on a disk that disappears at the next reboot, and nobody would notice until the data was gone.
- **Cost.** First install has one more manual step, listed in `docs/runbooks/deploy.md`.

### BD-06. Readiness reports check names, never causes
2026-10-17. `GET /api/ready` answers 200 or 503 with `{ready, checks[{name, ok}]}`. The cause of a failure goes to the server log. The route needs no session because the proxy and the deploy script call it.

### BD-07. Backups hold sealed credentials, the key travels separately
2026-10-17. `adx backup DIR` copies the database (SQLite `VACUUM INTO`) and the assets tree. The encryption key is never copied. The restore runbook rehearses in an isolated directory first. This is also the stance for every later secret: a copy of the data alone must be useless.

### BD-08. Web sign-in is OpenID Connect against authentik, sessions live in SQLite
2026-10-17. Implements D-24 for the web. `core/identity` owns sign-in attempts (hashed state, PKCE verifier, hashed nonce, 10-minute life, single use) and sessions (hashed random ID, 7 days idle, 30 days absolute, looked up on every request). `providers/authentik/oidc.go` does discovery, the code exchange with PKCE and client secret, RS256 verification and the nonce check, and reads `groups` from the ID token or userinfo. The `groups` claim must contain the configured group name (`ADX_AUTHENTIK_GROUP_NAME`, default `adx-users`) or `users.SignIn` refuses.

- **Why.** D-24 already chose authentik and database-backed sessions. A trusted-proxy header boundary was the alternative; it was rejected because the API and the web build are deployed separately and a header can be set by anyone who reaches the Go port.
- **Cost.** The authentik `adx-auth` provider needs the groups scope mapping enabled and the exact redirect URI `ADX_PUBLIC_URL/api/auth/callback`. Live sign-in is unverified until the provider's client ID and secret exist (see verification.md).
- **Not done.** MCP sign-in (ADX as an OAuth server for Claude, D-24) is not part of B0.3 and stays pending.

### BD-09. Actor carries a workspace; phase 0 has one
2026-10-17. `core.Actor` gains `WorkspaceID`, filled from the session's membership, never from the client. Migration 00006 creates workspace 1 "Reportage" (`core.DefaultWorkspace`) and a membership per existing user. While there is one workspace, `memberships.role` and `enabled` mirror `users.role` and `users.status`; `core/users` writes both in one transaction and ends the person's sessions when disabling them. New domains from B0.4 on scope their rows by `workspace_id` and refuse an actor whose workspace doesn't match. Existing tables (`projects`, `accounts`, `credentials`) stay unscoped until B6.1 migrates them.

- **Cost.** Two columns say the same thing until B6.1 drops the mirror. Recorded so the duplication is removed, not extended.

### BD-10. Policy is a versioned document; unconfigured denies every write
2026-10-17. `core/policies` stores the permission checklist, caps and per-account write enablement as one JSON document per workspace, with a new version on every save. `Evaluate(actor, request)` returns allowed, needs_approval or denied with a stable reason code and the policy version. Denial reasons in order: no workspace, role below marketer, unknown action, no policy document, kill switch (workspace or account), account not connected, account not enabled for writes, write capability not verified for the account, action unconfigured or off, cap unconfigured. D-13's table is exposed as `SuggestedDefaults` for an admin to apply deliberately; caps and write accounts stay empty in it, so applying it alone still denies.

- **Why.** The spec forbids inventing business policy and says a token existing never implies permission to write. Keeping the document versioned lets a later proposal name the version it was decided under.
- **Cost.** Until Abdul (or the CMO) sets caps and enables accounts, no write path can run, including in a demo. That is intended.

### BD-11. Capability state per account, health derived from it
2026-10-17. `account_capabilities` records each probe (`read.leads` for GoHighLevel so far) as verified, failed or needs_permission with a safe message. The accounts screen derives health: failed if any capability failed, needs_permission if any needs permission, stale if the last verification is older than 24 hours (engineering default), else connected. Health is never stored and no fixture account is ever shown.

### BD-12. Exported JSON types get unique names across core packages
2026-10-17. `gentypes` flattens every package into one TypeScript module, so `policies.Action` and `audit.Action` would merge into one wrong union. Types that cross the wire are named uniquely (`WriteAction`, `PolicyDocument`, `PolicyState`). Internal types can keep short names.

### BD-13. Runs are named by occurrence, leased by workers, never completed by a partial read
2026-10-17. `core/runs` keys each piece of durable work by `(workspace, kind, occurrence_key)`. Starting the same occurrence returns the existing run while it is queued, running or finished; a failed or interrupted run is requeued as a new attempt under the same reference. Workers lease the run and, when it names a provider account, the account, for 5 minutes between renewals. Every write by a worker is conditional on still holding the lease. `Finish` refuses `succeeded` unless completeness is `complete`. Recovery (startup and every minute) marks runs with expired leases `interrupted` and retries them up to 3 attempts, then leaves them for a person.

- **Why.** The spec requires stable occurrence keys, account leases and interrupted-run recovery, and that a partial read can't be called complete. Conditional writes make a dead worker's late writes harmless.
- **Cost.** A run kind must call `Progress` at least every 5 minutes or lose its lease. Long provider reads page, so that fits.

### BD-14. Evidence is versioned, never edited
2026-10-14. `core/evidence` keys an observation by `(workspace, source, kind, source_ref)`. Re-recording identical content is a no-op; different content inserts version n+1 and marks the old row superseded. Class is observed, estimated or inferred and completeness complete or partial, both required. Retention is unconfigured (`retain_until` null) and nothing is deleted.

### BD-15. River inserts the run's job in the run's transaction
2026-10-17. `jobs.Queue` implements `runs.Enqueuer` with River's `InsertTx` and a unique constraint on `run_id`, so a committed run always has exactly one live job and a rolled-back run has none. The job worker finds the run's executor by kind; unknown kinds fail the run visibly. Executors live outside `jobs` (phase 1 registers imports and refreshes in `cmd/adx`).

### BD-16. Creative behaviour is ported, not retained as a service
2026-10-17. The creative-studio app (`docs/build/reuse-creative.md`) is not run as a service beside ADX. Its layout document (`DesignDoc` v1), format table, copy blocks, house-rule checks and EN/AR handling are ported as `core/assets` types and, later, a React editor on the same document. Storage is `core/assets.Store`, implemented by `providers/filestore` (content-addressed by SHA-256 under `ADX_ASSETS_DIR`, written once, verified on read). Identity is ADX's session. Review is `assets.ReviewState` (draft → rendered → in_review → approved/revise); approved is terminal and a changed document is a new version with no approval. `ContentAcceptance.GrantsDelivery()` is always false: delivery authorization lives in the execution domain (B3.4).

- **Why.** The source has no immutability, no versions, anonymous approvals and Supabase identity, all of which the spec requires ADX to own. Its document model and rules are worth keeping.
- **Cost.** The canvas editor has to be rebuilt in ADX's React app (B1.6). The Python generator's contrast-aware placement is not ported.

### BD-17. Voice is three interfaces and a bridge, with fakes only
2026-10-17. `core/voice` declares `Telephony` (place/hang up/parse signed callbacks), `Transport` (one call's media frames, clear, mark) and `Speech` (conversation sessions). `voice.Bridge` ports the reference source's orchestration: codec check, queue engine audio in order, clear the far side on interruption, send an end mark and wait for its echo before closing, start timeout and maximum duration. No education rule, prompt or outcome enum is ported. `voicetest` fakes run the whole bridge with no credentials. Twilio and ElevenLabs adapters are not written in phase 0; the UAE telecom route is unchosen and unauthorized (blocker for B4.4). Ambience mixing and µ-law framing are deferred to B4.5.

### BD-18. D-27 recorded in docs/architecture.md
2026-10-17. The widening of scope the spec asks for is recorded as D-27 with the earlier decisions it changes marked, per the spec's instruction not to delete decision history. Live use of calling and messaging needs Reportage's written policy; the build does not.

### BD-19. Leads are provider contacts; the funnel is a versioned mapping that ships unconfigured
2026-10-17. `core/leads` keys a lead by `(account, GoHighLevel contact id)`. Nothing merges on phone or email: shared numbers are counted and shown, and person resolution is B4.1's. Every contact observation is evidence (`gohighlevel/contact`, versioned on content). The status, project and source are read through `FunnelDocument`, a versioned per-workspace mapping: where the status lives (custom field, contact field or tag prefix, because which CRM column holds it is open question #34), raw status → stage (catalog fixed in code: open, attempted, engaged, meeting, offer, won, disqualified, excluded, dead), blank status → stage, raw source → ADX source. Saving a new version re-stages every lead. With no mapping, status isn't located and stage stays null; with a mapping but an unmapped status, the raw value is kept and listed for the admin.

- **Why.** Reference.md says admins edit the status-to-stage table and ADX flags unmapped statuses; Hisham's table is a proposal, not a configured rule, so it is not seeded.
- **Status missing.** When a scan returns a contact without the configured status field, the last known status stays and `status_missing_since` records it (spec B1.2). Only a complete full scan marks unseen contacts removed; a failed or partial scan removes nothing, and a retry resumes from the recorded `searchAfter` cursor.
- **Campaign match.** Attribution records are graded by reference.md's match levels: a click id (gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbclid) is high, a platform campaign id medium, a hand-typed UTM campaign low. The campaign reference stays text until B1.3 has campaign rows to resolve it against.

### BD-20. GoHighLevel import uses POST /contacts/search with searchAfter
2026-10-17. From HighLevel's current docs (`scratchpad` research, 2026-10-17): `GET /contacts/` is deprecated and orders only by `dateAdded`; `POST /contacts/search` (API version 2021-07-28, Private Integration Token accepted) pages with the opaque `searchAfter` array each contact carries, which is the only way past 10,000 records. Full imports sort by `dateAdded, id`; incremental imports filter `dateUpdated` with a `range` and sort by it. Page size 100 (the API allows 500) to stay inside the 100-requests-per-10-seconds burst limit. Search results carry `firstNameLowerCase`/`lastNameLowerCase` rather than cased names, `customFields[].value` of any JSON type, and two attribution objects (`attributionSource`, `lastAttributionSource`) rather than an array. Webhooks need a Marketplace OAuth app, not a PIT, so contact deletes are detected only by full scans until an OAuth app exists.

- **Unconfirmed on the docs.** The `searchAfter` element shape (treated as opaque JSON), the `range` value shape for date filters (ISO-8601 strings assumed), and 429 behaviour (no `Retry-After` documented; the run fails safely and is retried). Live verification against the ADX Test location will confirm or correct these.

### BD-21. Google Ads and Meta are read through separate adapters written from current docs
2026-10-17. `providers/googleads` targets REST v26 with `searchStream` (unpaged JSON array of batches, int64 as strings, micros ÷ 1e6 to minor units, no developer token since the 2026-09-09 sunset, `login-customer-id` only through a manager). `providers/meta` targets Graph v26.0 (`/act_{id}/insights` at campaign level with `time_increment=1`; numbers are strings; `spend` is decimal major units and budgets are minor-unit strings, both normalized to minor units; `paging.next` followed only on the API host; the token travels in the Authorization header, never the URL). Each maps provider errors to safe `core.Error` messages with the provider's text and trace ids kept in the cause. Google's `conversions` and Meta's `lead` action are stored in different columns (`conversions`, `platform_leads`) and never summed. The doc-sourced facts are in `docs/build/api-notes/`; unconfirmed items (Meta lead node fields, Meta `/me/adaccounts` reference page, Google REST response cap) are listed there.

### BD-22. Ad platforms connect by OAuth, one credential per person, accounts discovered from the token
2026-10-17. `connections.StartAds/FinishAds` reuse the GoHighLevel attempt table (state, browser binding, 10 minutes) plus a PKCE verifier (migration 00011). After the exchange the signed-in person's stable id becomes the credential subject (D-26: one Google or Meta sign-in reaches many accounts). Accounts are discovered through the reader before anything is saved; a sign-in that reaches no accounts is refused; managers and businesses are parents, not accounts. Each discovered account gets `read.reporting` verified. `ProviderToken` refreshes a credential within five minutes of expiry (Google refresh token; Meta re-exchanges the long-lived token) and reseals it. Google's OAuth client and Meta's app are configuration (`ADX_GOOGLE_OAUTH_*`, `ADX_META_APP_*`); without them the connect buttons answer "not configured".

### BD-23. Refresh runs re-read a trailing window and record freshness per account
2026-10-17. `reporting.Execute` reads campaigns, then daily metrics page by page, then conversion actions, with progress after every page so a retry resumes at the cursor. Rows are replaced on re-read because both platforms revise recent days (Google: late conversions and invalid-traffic removals; Meta: up to 28 days). A range that includes the account's today is finished as `partial`, observed through yesterday. `account_freshness` holds last success, observed-through day, partial flag and last safe error; the connections screen shows it. A daily periodic job refreshes every connected ad account for the last `ADX_ADS_REFRESH_TRAILING_DAYS` (default 30). Metric rows for campaigns the campaign read did not return are counted (`unknownCampaignRows`) and skipped, never invented.

### BD-24. Metrics are deterministic, versioned and null-safe
2026-10-17. `reporting.Analytics` computes every figure in Go from stored rows under `FormulaVersion` v1: spend (minor units, null when currencies mix), impressions, clicks, Google conversions and Meta `lead` actions in separate fields that are never summed, GoHighLevel leads by the Dubai day they arrived, qualified leads and Done-Deals from the funnel stage (null without a funnel), cost per lead and per qualified lead as spend ÷ count (undefined on a zero count, null without spend), revenue and ROAS null until Done-Deal values arrive as a field (#35). Comparisons (previous period of the same length, same dates a year earlier, or custom) give absolute and relative change per metric; a zero or missing base makes the relative change undefined, never infinite. The summary is built from the same buckets as the rows so they reconcile by construction. Days with no rows for an account in scope are listed as missing, and the comparison period's gaps raise `comparison_incomplete`. Accounts outside Asia/Dubai are shown by calendar date with an `account_timezone_differs` warning because the platforms give no hourly data to re-cut a day.

### BD-25. Leads reach campaigns through their attribution's campaign reference; campaigns reach projects through their names
2026-10-17. A lead counts for a campaign when its first attribution's `matched_campaign_ref` equals the campaign's platform id or its name (case-insensitive). Click ids alone can't name a campaign without a click-to-campaign lookup, so they prove the platform but not the campaign until B3.3's measurement work. A campaign's project is read from its name: the project's words as whole words, a leading "The" optional (Reportage writes "Wadi" and "The Wadi"). A campaign naming two projects or none stays unassigned and is listed by `POST /api/analytics/assign-projects`, which also runs at the end of every refresh.

### BD-26. Reports are occurrences with frozen results; delivery needs recipients and a transport
2026-10-17. `core/reports` keys each report by schedule and period start (or by period and parameters for ad hoc requests), so a schedule tick that runs twice reuses the stored report and never sends it again. The stored `result` is the `ReportingResult` snapshot with its formula version and freshness, shown again exactly. Daily reports cover yesterday in Dubai, weekly the last Monday to Sunday, monthly the previous month, quarterly the previous quarter. Delivery is `unconfigured` with no recipients (the owner's input) or no SMTP host; `pending` → `sent`/`failed` is a conditional update so two deliverers can't both send. The email body is plain text rendered from the deterministic figures; "not available" and "no leads" are written out. A periodic job runs due schedules every six hours; the occurrence keys make extra ticks no-ops.

### BD-27. Anomaly checks ship with no thresholds and never act
2026-10-17. `core/alerts` keeps a versioned per-workspace configuration for three checks: cost spike (percent above the campaign's average over the days it ran in a baseline window, with a minimum spend and a minimum of three baseline days so a campaign that ran once has no baseline), zero leads (spend above a minimum on a day whose figures are complete with no lead in GoHighLevel), stale ingestion (no complete figures newer than a maximum age). With no configuration no check runs; with a null threshold that check skips. A day whose figures are not complete raises nothing but a skip note and, if configured, a stale-ingestion alert: no figures is not zero leads. The same check firing for the same subject while its alert is open adds an occurrence, and the same day is never counted twice. Every alert message ends "No change was made": alerts observe; proposals (B3.4) act.

### BD-28. The assistant reads through an allowlist, and every number is checked against tool results
2026-10-17. `core/assistant` owns the conversation loop: the model proposes tool calls, deterministic code runs only the four allowlisted read tools (`get_analytics`, `get_lead_coverage`, `list_alerts`, `get_connections`) with the asking person's actor, validates each input against the tool's schema before running it, and feeds results back as data. A tool name outside the allowlist, whoever or whatever asked for it (the person, the model, or text inside a tool result), is refused with a message saying the assistant cannot change budgets, campaigns, leads or settings; there is no write tool and no path to the policy evaluator or proposals. The final answer is scanned for numbers; any number that appears in no tool result (allowing thousands separators, minor-unit rounding, years and dates) is flagged `ungrounded_numbers`, and an answer with numbers but no tool call is flagged `no_tool_evidence`. The screen shows these as unverified. Each turn stores the model, tokens, cost (null unless prices are configured), evidence refs and warnings. Model failures become an `unavailable` turn with a safe message and a `retryable` flag; refusals become `refused`; neither is replayed to the model as history. Limits: 6 tool rounds per question, 4000 output tokens per call, a daily token budget per workspace (default 2M).

### BD-29. Claude through the official Go SDK is the one production adapter
2026-10-17. `providers/anthropic` implements `assistant.Model` with the Anthropic Go SDK (Messages API, tools as `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks, thinking left at the model's adaptive default, `output_config.effort` from configuration). Default model `claude-opus-5-5`, effort `medium`, 120 s timeout, two retries. API errors map to retryable (429, 5xx, 529, timeouts, network) or not (401/403: key; 400/404: configuration) with safe messages; the provider's text and ids stay in the cause. The key, model name, base URL, effort, timeout, budget and prices are `ADX_MODEL_*` settings; none exists on this machine, so live calls are unverified. Server-side refusal fallbacks (`fallbacks`) are not enabled: a refusal is recorded as a refused turn, which is the conservative choice for a read-only assistant; this is a configuration to revisit with the owner.

### BD-30. Creative pilot: SVG template renderer, review bound to output checksum, text-only editor
2026-10-17. `core/creative` ports the creative source's layout rules as `assets.Layout` (logo top centre under the 9:16 keep-clear zone, text block above the bottom zone, Arabic right-aligned and right-to-left with Arabic fonts) and its house-rule checks as `assets.CheckDocument`; errors block rendering. `providers/svgrender` renders a document to a deterministic SVG with embedded images, labelled `template`; the SVG is the immutable output whose checksum review binds to. Submitting is putting the version on the review board; approval records the output checksum and produces a `ContentAcceptance` that never grants delivery. Editing a draft is in place; editing anything rendered, in review, approved or sent back creates the next draft version with no approval. Export streams the stored bytes after verifying the checksum. Files are served with a sandboxing content security policy and `nosniff` because SVG can carry script. The web editor changes text and vertical position; the canvas drag editor and pixel export are B3.1.

- **Why.** The pilot needs the journey end to end with the invariants the spec names (approval invalidated by edits, board ≠ delivery, no fixtures). An SVG renderer is deterministic, testable and needs no font files on the server; the browser rasterizes it.
- **Cost.** Visual fidelity of long Arabic copy is unverified until someone looks at it in a browser (recorded in `pilot-gate.md`). Rasterized exports for ad platforms wait for B3.1.

### BD-31. Brand facts: classified by provenance, conflicts block approval, scope is the brand
2026-10-17. `core/brands` owns brands (ours or competitor), the project-to-brand assignment (a nullable `brand_id` on `projects`, existing ids kept), offers as immutable versions with effective dates, and facts as single assertions with effective dates. A fact's class says where it came from: `needs_review` (a person entered it), `inferred` (ADX derived it from a named evidence row; only the job actor may write one), `approved` (an admin signed it off), `retired` (history, with the reason). Only approved facts become claims. Two current facts for the same key and scope with different values and overlapping dates open a conflict; a fact in an open conflict cannot be approved, and resolving a conflict retires the loser without approving the winner. A project fact beside a brand-wide fact is not a conflict; the project's wins for that project. Offers are approved as "true as written" and the approval never carries to a new version; revising an offer lists the creatives built on older versions as affected and changes none of them. A creative takes an offer only from its project's brand, and a render uploaded for a project only on that project. The brand kit route moved to `/api/projects/{id}/brand-kit` to free `/api/brands` for brands.

- **Why.** The spec's gate (contradictory sources need review; a changed offer names what it affects; another brand's evidence never reaches a draft) is about provenance and scope, so both are explicit columns, not conventions. Source precedence is an unresolved business rule, so nothing resolves a conflict but an admin.
- **Cost.** Every fact is a row and every claim lookup is a query per key; fine at Reportage's scale. Facts have no numeric comparison (a "from" price of 1,200,000 and 1,200,001 conflict), which is the point.

### BD-32. Research: every retrieval is an item, the network boundary is one package, estimates stay labelled
2026-10-17. `core/research` holds briefs (a question about a brand or project) made of items: pages to read, competitor pages, keyword seeds, our own account audit. A run works each pending item once and records either findings with an evidence row or a safe failure on the item; a source that didn't answer produces no finding. Findings carry a scope (`account` for our own figures, `public` for anything off the web) and the evidence class (`observed`, `estimated`); the two scopes are listed apart and never summed. Keyword Planner volumes and bids are `estimated` and say so in their payload. A competitor typed by name resolves only on an exact match with a competitor brand; a partial match or none leaves the item in `needs_identity` with the candidates listed, nothing is fetched for it, and no brand is created from a typed name. `providers/webfetch` is the only code that fetches a URL someone typed: http/https on the standard ports, no credentials in the URL, the host resolved and every answer checked against loopback, private, link-local, multicast, carrier-NAT, documentation and IPv4-mapped ranges, the connection pinned to the approved address, redirects re-checked, bodies capped and reduced to text. Nothing in a page is followed or interpreted: links, meta refreshes and instructions are text in an evidence row. A refusal is final; an unavailable source is retried on the next run. Briefs refuse an address the fetcher would refuse so the person sees it at once.

- **Why.** The spec's gates are about not inventing (statistics, identities) and not being steered (private network, injected text). Making every retrieval a row with a state makes gaps visible instead of filled, and keeping fetching in one package makes the boundary auditable.
- **Cost.** Competitor ad observation has no API route for the UAE (Meta's Ad Library API returns only political ads outside the EU), so competitor research is pages a person names. Keyword ideas need a Google Ads account and ride on its OAuth; the request shape is unverified live (api-notes). The web extractor is regex-based, good enough for text, not a DOM.

### BD-33. Plans: immutable validated versions, acceptance without spend, exact template gated
2026-10-17. `core/plans` stores a plan's versions as immutable JSON documents typed in Go: allocations by channel from a fixed catalog (`Channels`, each marked supported or manual), asset, page and measurement requirements, test hypotheses, observation windows, evidence references and assumptions classed assumption, unavailable or cited. Saving validates in code and stores the result with the version; the state is `ready` with no blocking issue, `needs_input` when a required input is missing, `invalid` when what is there contradicts itself (allocations not totalling the budget, an unknown channel, a reference to evidence that doesn't exist, a dangling citation, a project of another brand). An admin accepts a `ready` version; acceptance is terminal for that version, `GrantsSpend` is always false and `ExecutionAuthorization` is always null in this domain. Any edit is the next version with no acceptance. Export and import go through `TemplateAdapter`s: JSON (whole document, lossless) and CSV (allocation table with the plan header) always; the exact Excel adapter is absent, `Templates()` says why and what unblocks it, and `format=xlsx` is a 409 with that reason, never a 500 or a generic file dressed as the template.

- **Why.** The spec's gates for this task are arithmetic that can't drift, acceptance that isn't permission, and an exact-template capability that is reported blocked rather than faked.
- **Cost.** The CSV form drops requirements and assumptions, which is stated in its test and in the UI's wording. The channel catalog is ADX's, not Reportage's agency's; unsupported channels can be planned and are flagged manual.

### BD-34. Plan generation: the model fills a frame, code pins it, nothing generated is accepted
2026-10-17. `plans.Generate` asks the configured model for the next version of a plan by forcing one tool call (`propose_plan`, `assistant.Request.ToolChoice`, mapped to the Messages API `tool_choice` with parallel calls off) whose schema has no budget, currency or period and whose channel enum holds only channels ADX can deploy. The context is the plan's frame, the findings of the research briefs named (same brand only), the brand's approved claims and current offers; those ids are the only evidence a proposal may cite. Code then pins the frame back, drops evidence refs that weren't in the context, turns a cited assumption whose reference was dropped into `unavailable`, blanks every expected cost per lead that no cited `cpl.<channel>` assumption backs and records it as unavailable, rejects the whole proposal on an unknown or undeployable channel (nothing saved), and runs the same validator as a hand-written version. The result is a `generated` version in the ordinary state machine; acceptance stays an admin's act. Every call is an evidence row (`adx/plan_generation`, usage and a request hash, not the prompt) and the workspace has a daily cap (default 40). `Diff` compares two versions field by field and allocation by allocation and, when the earlier one is accepted, names it as superseded in content; the acceptance record itself is never changed. Offers report the plan versions that cite them next to the creatives built on them.

- **Why.** The spec's gates: an unsupported channel from the model is rejected, a revision can't mutate an accepted version, content acceptance isn't permission to spend, and a missing CPC estimate stays an assumption or unavailable. Making the frame the team's and the evidence a closed set keeps the model to distributing and citing.
- **Cost.** Downstream references are computed (offers → plans, accepted → superseded), not stored as a graph; phase 3's assets, pages and proposals will reference plan versions directly. The generation cap is per workspace per day, separate from Ask ADX's token budget.

### BD-35. Recurring research: refresh runs, comparative reports, hypotheses that stay hypotheses
2026-10-17. A research schedule (weekly, monthly or quarterly; never daily) re-reads a brief's sources in a `refresh` run and then writes one comparative report per period, keyed on the brief and the period. The report puts observed things side by side: our account against the previous period through the reporting engine (recorded as evidence), each competitor page against its previous evidence version (changed or not, both excerpts), each keyword estimate against the last run (labelled Google's estimate), and the market events a person recorded. Hypotheses are generated deterministically, one per overlapping recorded event, per changed competitor page, per keyword estimate that moved by at least a fifth; each cites the evidence rows it rests on, is classed `hypothesis` and carries `causal: false`. No model is involved. With no account history the report is `limited`, states why, and its hypotheses say there is nothing to correlate with. Market events are evidence a marketer records with a source; ADX has no calendar of festivals or economic dates, because which events matter to Reportage's buyers is the team's knowledge and a built-in list would be a guess presented as fact. Operators review hypotheses (`accepted`, `rejected`, `corrected` with the corrected explanation); the review sits beside the hypothesis and the next period's report lists the previous report's hypotheses with their reviews. `RunDue` advances each enabled schedule one step per tick (start the refresh, then write the report once the run has ended), so one period gets one run and one report.

- **Why.** The gates: lack of history produces a limited audit; a festival or economic explanation needs cited evidence and remains a hypothesis; a repeat run keeps the prior report's context. Deterministic generation keeps the explanations to what the evidence can carry.
- **Cost.** Hypotheses are coarse (period-level correlation). Competitor "changes" are any text change on the page, including a date in a footer; the excerpts let a person judge. The evaluation cases are the tests (a brand with history and a brand without), not a stored fixture set.

### BD-36. Production creatives: renders as runs, provenance on every file, claims checked against approved facts
2026-10-17. Rendering is a durable run (`creative.render`, one per version and document hash); the worker writes the content-addressed file first and updates the row in one guarded statement, so a failure between the two leaves an orphan file at most and a retry lands on the same key. The version keeps the last safe render error. Every asset row carries `provenance` (`uploaded`, `template_render`, `ai_generated`); `assets.ImageGenerator` is an interface with no provider, `Capabilities()` says so, and the page says "AI image generation: not configured". A creative may be tied to a plan version and to an offer version; at render time `bindClaims` reads every percentage and price in the copy (Latin and Arabic digits) and checks it against the brand's approved claims and the approved offer the creative was built on, storing the result as `bindings`. `Readiness` re-runs that check against today's facts and blocks on unapproved content, an unapproved or changed offer, any unapproved figure, or a missing output; Arabic copy warns that native review is not recorded. The web page is a queue by state, a drag canvas over the render, a side-by-side compare of any two versions with their reviews, and the readiness verdict.

- **Why.** The gates: an old approval can't cover a new image (unchanged from B1.6 and re-asserted by readiness), partial failures recover, a template layout is never advertised as AI generation, and unapproved claims fail launch readiness. Reading the copy for figures is the only way to catch a claim nobody approved without trusting the writer to list them.
- **Cost.** The claim reader catches percentages and prices only; a handover date or unit count is not checked and the panel says a claim it can't read is not judged. Pixel export is still the browser's job.

### BD-37. Landing pages: structured documents served by ADX, forms scoped to page version and project, tests never customers
2026-10-17. `core/pages` stores a page as versions of a structured document (headline, sections of fixed kinds, an optional bound offer version, a form definition); there is no raw HTML field. The server renders a version with `html/template`, which escapes everything an editor typed, and serves it under a content security policy with no script source at all; the editor's preview adds `sandbox` and is shown in a sandboxed frame. ADX hosts pages at `/p/{slug}` through a `Publisher` interface whose only implementation is local; an adapter for Reportage's Wix or WordPress sites is not written, because the hosts and access are unknown, and the gate says so. A deployment names the exact version and the output checksum; a rollback is a new deployment naming the deployment it rolled back from, so the restored version is on record. The public form post is scoped: the page's project, never the posted one, is what the submission is recorded against, and a post naming another project is rejected and recorded as rejected; fields are validated against the form definition; a honeypot, a per-address rate limit and a per-page daily cap stand in front of the database; attribution keeps only UTM, click ids, referrer and landing. The page's secret test token marks a submission as the team's test; test rows never count as enquiries. Readiness requires a live page, a form with a required email or phone that is placed on the page, a successful test submission on the live version itself, an approved and current offer, and approved claims in the copy (the brand's `CheckCopy`, shared with creatives).
- **Why.** The gates: a broken form can't pass readiness, a wrong-project submission is rejected, a rollback identifies the exact old version, untrusted content can't run script in the editor. Requiring a test on the live version means readiness is about the thing visitors reach, not a draft.
- **Cost.** Pages are plain: no custom styling beyond the template, no analytics scripts (B3.3 adds measurement through the server, not through third-party tags). Image sections reference asset keys but there is no public asset route yet; an image section renders a broken image until B3.3 decides which assets may be public.

### BD-38. Measurement: one event per submission, tests never count, readiness never says live
2026-10-17. `core/measurement` keeps an event catalog in code that says what ADX counts (form submissions on its own pages, server side; CRM stages through the funnel) and what it cannot (page views, WhatsApp and call clicks: pages carry no client script by policy and there is no tag or call tracking), each with the reason. A received form submission becomes exactly one event, keyed on its submission id; a repeat of the same person (last nine phone digits or the email) on the same page within a day is marked a duplicate and does not count; a test submission is a test event that never counts. Checks are controlled verifications recorded with evidence: a form check posts a real test submission through the page's own form path with the page's test token and passes only when exactly one non-counting test event resulted and the enquiry count did not move; a conversion-action check reads the account's last Google Ads refresh and fails on a missing, removed or excluded action; a Meta pixel check is recorded as unsupported, because ADX has no Pixel or Conversions API integration; an account check reads connection health. Links are built with one fixed UTM scheme (`plan-<id>-v<version>-<channel>`, `creative-<id>-v<version>`). `Readiness` joins the accepted plan version, the creatives bound to it against its asset requirements, the pages bound to it, a connected account per platform planned, a passed check per measurement requirement and a passed form check, and lists what is unsupported; it carries `live: false` and no execution authorization, and names platform review as not started.

- **Why.** The gates: one test submission records one intended enquiry (a test one, counted as nothing), unsupported tracking is explicit, a pending external review is not ready or live, and verification fabricates no customer event. Posting the real form path for the check means readiness measures the path visitors take.
- **Cost.** Events exist only for ADX pages and CRM stages; a lead that arrives through a Meta lead form or a portal is an analytics row, not a measurement event, until B4.1's enquiry model. Readiness blocks on a connected account per platform, which this machine has none of, so the readiness journey is proven in tests up to that gate.

### BD-39. Proposals: authority checked at the moment of acting, approval bound to the target's version, budget reserved in one transaction
2026-10-17. `core/proposals` records every intended change to an outside account as a typed proposal: the target's kind, reference and observed version, what it is now and what it should become, the reason, evidence refs, the amount it would spend and the envelope that allows it, and the policy decision with its version and reason. Policy is evaluated at proposal, again at approval and again at execution; a denied evaluation is recorded as a denied proposal, never dropped. An approval binds to the target version it saw; `Observe` marks live proposals stale when a refresh sees the target changed, and execution refuses an approval that doesn't cover the current version. A budget envelope is one allocation of an accepted plan version tied to an account; executing reserves from it and writes the execution intent in a single write transaction with no provider call inside, so two reservations cannot both take the same remainder (tested with ten racing goroutines). An intent that has not left the outbox can be cancelled and its reservation released. Every write path refuses `core.ViaAssistant`, which the assistant now stamps on the actor it hands its tools, and the assistant's allowlist is checked for anything that is not a read.

- **Why.** The gates: no double reservation, no execution without configured authority, a changed target invalidates its approval, and the read-only assistant cannot reach the executor. Checking authority when acting rather than remembering it means a kill switch or a policy change takes effect at once.
- **Cost.** Envelopes are opened by hand from an accepted plan; nothing opens them automatically. Dispatch, provider refs and reconciliation are B3.5; until then every intent sits in the outbox as `reserved`.

### BD-40. Execution: authority re-checked at dispatch, uncertainty reconciled by marker before any retry, submission is not delivery
2026-10-17. `core/execution` is the only code that writes to an ad account. A platform `Writer` declares the actions it implements; Google Ads and Meta each implement four (create a paused campaign, raise and lower a campaign budget, pause a campaign) from the current REST references, and nothing else is claimed: a proposal for any other action fails as not implemented. Writers are registered only when `ADX_LIVE_WRITES=1`; otherwise every intent is held in the outbox with that reason and nothing is sent, which is how fake-provider tests run against a server whose live accounts stay disabled. Before each dispatch the policy is evaluated again, so a kill switch or a withdrawn enablement holds anything not yet sent. Every object ADX creates carries `[adx:<intent id>]` in its name; a transport failure or 5xx after a request leaves the intent `uncertain`, and before any retry it is looked up by that marker, so a timeout after a real create is found and recorded rather than created again. `submitted` means the platform accepted the request; `externally_confirmed` means a later read found the object and its status; neither is delivery, which is read from the platform's own figures (B3.6). A launch across platforms is `partial` while any platform failed and is never `confirmed` until every one is; a failed intent releases its reservation, a submitted one consumes it. Every transition is an event on the intent's timeline.

- **Why.** The gates: no duplicate on retry after a timeout, partial stays partial, submission is not confirmed delivery, and an unauthorized live account stays disabled while fakes run. Marker-based lookup is the only honest answer to "did it land?" when the platform gives no idempotency key.
- **Cost.** The write surface is small by design; keywords, audiences, exclusions, ad sets, ads and creatives are not written. Request shapes are tested against fakes of the documented responses and are unverified live.

### BD-41. Recovery and compensation: interrupted sends become uncertain, reversal stops spend and says what it cannot do, delivery is impressions
2026-10-17. An intent found in `dispatching` after a restart is not sent again: `RecoverInterrupted` makes it `uncertain` with the reason, and the ordinary marker lookup settles whether the request landed. The kill switch holds anything not yet sent, including what recovery put back. Compensation runs through the proposal path, so it is policy-checked, recorded and dispatched like any change: a created campaign is paused (it was created paused; it stays on the platform for a person to remove), a budget change is set back to what the proposal recorded as current, a pause is not reversed by ADX because resuming would restart spend. `Reversibility` tells the operator what reversal can do per state and reports what the intent's reservation consumed; neither it nor the compensation detail ever describes spent money as recovered, refunded or undone. A refused intent is repaired as a new proposal that points back at it. Milestones are read from records: plan acceptance, first send, first platform acceptance, first confirmation, and delivery as the first day with impressions in the platform's own figures for the campaign ADX created; the one-hour mark is met only when that delivery is observed within an hour of acceptance, and the note says so otherwise.

- **Why.** The gates: a restart resumes safely across the dispatch boundary, the kill switch prevents undispatched actions, spent money is never described as undone, and the one-hour aspiration is not reported achieved without delivery evidence.
- **Cost.** Compensation covers the four implemented actions only. The approved test-account journey against a live account was not run: no account is enabled for writes, no test account exists here and no written approval was given, so that gate stays external.

### BD-42. People are resolved conservatively: exact identifiers only, shared phones are candidates, every link and merge is reversible, and the customer's word outranks a provider's guess
2026-10-17. A person is who; an enquiry is a project they asked about, so one person carries several enquiries and the same person asking about a second project is a new enquiry, not a new person. Resolution links each CRM lead and each non-test form submission to a person with the evidence it used: an email held by exactly one person is exact; a phone is exact only when exactly one of its holders has a name that agrees; anything else (a phone shared by several people, a holder whose name differs, an email held by several) creates a new person and a match candidate per partial match, so the uncertainty is on the record and visible, not resolved by a guess. A candidate is decided by a marketer: accept merges, reject closes. Links can be reversed with a reason, merges can be undone from the merge record, manual links are allowed when the record is not already linked. Attributes carry their class: what the customer stated, what an enrichment provider inferred. An enriched value never replaces a stated one; it sits beside it and the view flags the conflict. Enrichment runs only through a provider that declares its name, cost and permitted attributes, only for the intersection of the provider's list and ADX's own permitted list, and every run is evidence of class inferred with the cost and the dropped keys. No provider is wired.

- **Why.** The gates: a shared family phone is not auto-merged, a conflicting enrichment does not overwrite a customer-stated fact, no exact match leaves uncertainty visible.
- **Cost.** Resolution runs every ten minutes and on demand; it does not re-match records already linked, so a changed name on a lead does not move it. Name agreement is token overlap after normalisation, so transliteration variants of the same Arabic name are candidates rather than exact matches.

### BD-43. Signals score only confirmed people, under versioned rules, with the reasons on record
2026-10-17. An interaction event is stored once per source and occurrence key, so a webhook delivered twice is one event and one assessment. Identity is resolved only through exact identifiers that all point at the same person; a device or browser id alone, a phone shared by several people, or an email and a phone that name different people leave the event `unknown`, visible on the scoring page, and excluded from every score until a marketer attributes it by hand. Scoring rules are a versioned document: per-kind points, half-life, repeat damping and cap for intent; attribute-to-points for fit, stated values preferred; stage thresholds for temperature. Fit and intent add, so a person with no fit attributes has intent and "fit not available", never zero (D-17). With no rules saved, the assessment still records that rules were missing; with no stage thresholds, nobody is hot, warm or cold. Every assessment keeps the rules version and a full explanation (contributions, exclusions, previous temperature), and corrections (discard, reattribute) are rows of their own that re-assess the people affected and leave the earlier assessments standing. Derived events come from records ADX already holds: a linked form submission, and a CRM status that differs from the last status recorded for that lead. The GoHighLevel webhook adapter is public and requires a configured shared secret; it scores opportunity stage updates and inbound messages and acknowledges other types as ignored.

- **Why.** The gates: a repeated webhook scores once, unknown cross-device identity is never a confident signal, unconfigured stage criteria classify nobody, corrections re-evaluate with history.
- **Cost.** Website page views need a tracked-link token to carry an identity (the voice source's identity bridge is not ported yet); until then every page view arrives as unknown. The per-kind rule shapes are the voice source's; the point values in the suggested document are placeholders an admin must confirm.

### BD-44. Outreach: a rule-based next step from the brief, a field-owned CRM outbox that tells echoes from edits, drafts from approved facts, and nothing sent until a channel is configured
2026-10-17. The sales brief for an enquiry gathers the person, the project's approved facts, the open objections, contact preferences and opt-outs, the latest score, drafts and CRM field writes, and recommends one step by a fixed rule: a closed enquiry or a do-not-contact preference or an all-channel opt-out stops; a waiting draft is the step; an open objection that an approved fact answers is a message with a draft quoting that fact, otherwise a call; hot and quiet a day is a call; quiet under two days waits; seven days of silence is a follow-up message. Drafts are checked against approved facts and an unapproved figure holds the draft so it cannot be approved. Sending needs, in order: the person not suppressed on the channel, an outreach configuration with the channel mode on, a wired messaging adapter that serves the channel, Dubai quiet hours over, and an address on record; a retry runs the same checks, so an opt-out recorded after approval still stops the send. Lifting an opt-out is admin-only and needs the renewed consent on record. The CRM field outbox holds one row per value ADX wants a field to have; the import reports every contact's custom fields to it: the same value is an echo that confirms the row, a different value is a conflict when ADX owns the field, supersedes the row when the CRM owns it, and is a conflict for a person when ownership is unconfigured. Nothing observed ever creates a write. Dispatch needs the field owned by ADX, the `ghl.lead_fields.set` policy allowed for the account with a verified `write.lead_fields` capability, a field writer (the GoHighLevel client, only with `ADX_LIVE_WRITES`) and a token; anything missing holds the row with the reason.

- **Why.** The gates: an outside edit racing ADX becomes a conflict or follows configured ownership, a provider echo creates no new intent, a suppressed person cannot be contacted by retry, automatic messaging stays off until policy is configured.
- **Cost.** The "automatic" channel mode is accepted but behaves as "approved": no messaging policy has been supplied, so this build never sends without a person's approval, and the config view never claims automatic. No messaging adapter exists; the `Messenger` contract is the seam. Draft text is a template, not a model, so it is plain; a model-written draft would still have to pass the same claim check.

### BD-45. Calls fail closed: an authorized route, a passed contactability check and an atomic reservation before any phone rings; unknown results are reconciled, not retried
2026-10-17. The calling policy is a versioned document: the telecom route (provider, who authorized it, when), consent requirement, Dubai calling window, concurrent lines, attempts per enquiry per day, caller number and recording (on/off, retention days, access role). Live calling needs all of: a policy, a named route, written authorization, a wired adapter whose name is the route's, and a caller number; the state view lists what is missing.
