A call request runs the contactability checks (closed enquiry, workspace kill switch, phone on record, call opt-out, do-not-contact, consent basis, hours, capacity, daily attempts, an active or unknown call for the enquiry) and refuses with every reason; then one transaction re-counts capacity and active calls and inserts the row under a unique occurrence key, so simultaneous requests ring once. The provider is asked only after the row exists; its error leaves the call `unknown`, which blocks further attempts until `Reconcile` asks the provider: found applies the provider's state, not found after a grace period is `failed` with "nothing was placed". Callbacks are verified by the adapter (a bad signature is 403 and records nothing), matched to a call ADX placed, applied in order with redeliveries and out-of-order earlier states ignored and late events after a terminal state recorded but not applied. Recordings are deleted at the provider after the policy's retention and marked, keeping the reference; access needs the policy's role. `providers/twilio` is a reference transport: calls connect a media stream to ADX and hang up when it ends, callbacks are checked with Twilio's HMAC-SHA1 signature over the public URL, lookups and recording deletion use the REST API. It is wired only when `ADX_TELECOM_ROUTE=twilio`.

- **Why.** The gates: simultaneous requests cannot launch a duplicate call, an unknown result reconciles before a repeat, no chosen and authorized route blocks live calling but not fake-route tests, an invalid webhook is rejected.
- **Cost.** The UAE telecom route is not chosen and Reportage's position on automated calls ("not open") has not been reversed in writing; both stay blockers for live calling. Twilio is a reference, not a recommendation. The media stream endpoint the TwiML points at is B4.5's.

### BD-46. A call's reading is evidence first, fact second: transcripts are kept, the model's reading is applied once per version and only when trusted, uncertain figures are held, corrections re-apply with history
2026-10-17. The media stream is accepted only when the provider's start message names the call SID ADX placed and carries the call's occurrence key; anything else is closed before audio. The conversation runs through `voice.Bridge` with the agent's leg optionally mixed over a generated room tone and framed at 20 ms, so a barge-in clears at most one frame. The agent's brief comes from the sales brief: the project, the approved facts it may quote exactly, the five questions, and the rule that any other figure is for the team to confirm. The transcript is stored on the session and as observed evidence. The reading is a forced structured tool call: outcome, answers each with a quote and an uncertainty flag, objections, requested human, callback time, confidence. Low confidence or no model leaves the reading `pending`; nothing is applied until a person confirms or corrects it. Application is one version under `call:<id>:v<n>`: a scoring signal for interested, not interested, callback or transfer (no-answer, voicemail, wrong number and unclear score nothing), stated attributes for answers the model was sure of, a stage for a clear outcome; an answer marked uncertain is held and named, never written. Objections are recorded whatever the confidence, with the call as their source. A correction stores the person's reading, discards the earlier scoring event with the reason, and applies again as the next version, so the history keeps both. Recordings are served only to the role the calling policy names, never after retention deleted them. `providers/elevenlabs` speaks the Conversational AI WebSocket protocol, refuses an agent not set to `ulaw_8000`, overrides only the prompt and first message, answers pings and ends when the agent closes.

- **Why.** The gates: an interruption clears queued stale speech, an uncertain number or price does not assert a stage change, a repeated completion duplicates neither task nor score, recording access and retention follow the configured policy.
- **Cost.** The stage names written (`qualified`, `not_interested`, `callback`, `handoff`) are ADX's; they are not mapped to GoHighLevel's pipeline until Reportage names its stages. No live call has run; the ElevenLabs protocol is tested against documented shapes only.

### BD-47. Speech to ADX is a transcript through the same read-only tools, previewed before anything happens; quality is measured against the team's labels and predictive claims stay off until the evidence exists
2026-10-17. The operator's voice mode is the browser's speech recognition feeding the assistant a transcript: the text is shown back before it is sent, the turn is marked as spoken, and a reading of the words names anything that sounds like a change (budget, pause, launch, bids, messages, calls, approvals, record edits) with the figures as heard. That preview is information, not permission: the assistant answers through the same allowlisted read tools as typing, a write-shaped tool call is refused as before, and no proposal is created from speech. The lead-facing agent (B4.5) and the operator interface share nothing but the `voice` package's codec helpers; one speaks to customers through a telecom route, the other listens to the operator in the browser. The evaluation ledger keeps one agreed label per call, recorded by a person apart from the model's reading and from corrections, and reports: agreement of the model's first reading with labels, correction rate, pending share, alert states and resolution, and observed feedback (objections, opt-outs, held and sent drafts, field conflicts, signal corrections). Every rate is null with nothing to divide by. Predictive claims are gated on at least 50 labelled calls with at least 80% agreement; below that the gate reports what is missing, and nothing in ADX phrases a prediction.

- **Why.** The gates: an ambiguous spoken budget cannot silently execute a write, qualification quality is measured against agreed labels, predictive claims stay disabled without sufficient evaluation evidence.
- **Cost.** The action preview is keyword-based and will both miss and over-name; it never decides anything, so a miss costs only a missing warning. Speech recognition is the browser's, so Arabic quality depends on the browser; the transcript is editable before sending. No evaluation figure has real data behind it yet.

### BD-48. The native pipeline is one opportunity per enquiry with an owned stage; imports preview everything and change nothing until applied, resume where they stopped, and never move a stage a person set when ADX owns it
2026-10-17. An opportunity belongs to one enquiry, so a person asking about two projects has two independent opportunities with their own stage, owner, tasks and interactions. The stage catalogue is a versioned configuration (key, label, kind open/won/lost; a lead-stage map; a stage owner). Every stage move carries who set it (user, import, system) and bumps the record's version; a move with a stale version is refused, so two people editing one record collide instead of overwriting. An import preview plans a row per enquiry against the linked lead's funnel stage (create, update stage, skip with the reason, or conflict) and writes only the plan. Apply walks the plan from its cursor, one transaction per row, marking each applied, so a failure resumes and a repeat adds nothing; creates are idempotent on the enquiry; a configuration change between preview and apply refuses the apply. Ownership is re-checked on the live record at apply time: with ADX as stage owner a stage a person set stays however the CRM moves, with the CRM as owner the import moves it and records that the import did. Provider mappings tie each opportunity to its GoHighLevel contact id both ways, and the export lists them so the CRM can be reconciled against ADX. Follow-up tasks are created once per occurrence key (a repeated "call back Tuesday" is one task); interactions attach to the person and at most one opportunity and are evidence.

- **Why.** The gates: a repeated import creates no duplicate opportunity, customer corrections survive sync according to ownership, multiple enquiries per person remain independent, a migration preview does not mutate records.
- **Cost.** The import source is ADX's own enquiries and leads; a direct GoHighLevel opportunities read is not written, because Reportage's pipeline stages are unknown. The pipeline stages written by qualification (`qualified`, `callback`…) are enquiry stages, not pipeline stages, until the owner maps them.

### BD-49. The registry grants nothing its saver does not hold: versions are immutable drafts, wider access and model-written drafts wait for an admin, tools come from a fixed catalogue with no direct write, and outputs are checked against the skill's own schema
2026-10-17. A skill is instructions, an input and an output schema (a JSON-Schema subset ADX can check), an evidence scope (public, account, project, brand, person) and permitted tools. The capability catalogue is fixed in code: the assistant's read tools, domain reads, and three "propose" capabilities that create proposals or drafts for a person and policy to decide; there is no capability that writes to an outside system. An agent bundles active skills under an account scope of connected accounts, holds no tools of its own (its tools are the union of its skills'), and a super agent coordinates agents and holds no skills. A workflow definition is a bounded graph: every step names one active agent or skill, dependencies exist, there is no cycle, loops have a maximum of at most 20, the total executions fit `maxSteps`, and a step whose skill proposes changes must be marked external. Every save is a new immutable draft version with its validation problems stored; activation needs no problems and retires the previous active version. A draft needs an admin when a model proposed it (the assistant's actor, or the caller says so), when it is a first version with any tools or scope saved by a marketer, when it adds tools, widens the evidence scope, adds skills, adds accounts or coordinates more agents than the active version, or when a workflow step is external; a marketer may activate a version that only changes instructions. The model's own actor can never activate.

- **Why.** The gates: a prompt edit cannot expand account access, a malformed output fails schema validation, a generated skill remains a draft until the required authority accepts it.
- **Cost.** The schema subset covers type, required, properties, additionalProperties, enum, items, bounds and lengths; patterns, formats and references are not supported, and a skill declaring them is refused rather than half-checked. The registry does not yet execute anything; B5.3 runs the graphs.

### BD-50. Workflows are durable graphs whose only outside effect is a proposal: leases resume, external steps act once under an operation key, changed upstream results invalidate downstream ones without re-firing anything external, loops and budgets are bounded
2026-10-17. A run is built from an active definition (checked again for cycles and bounds) as one task per step; tasks become ready when their dependencies are done and are leased one at a time, with attempts counted and a lease that expires back to ready, so a crashed worker's task resumes. A step's input is the run's parameters plus its dependencies' outputs, hashed with their versions; a done task's output carries a version. Correcting a task's output bumps the version and invalidates everything downstream: read-only dependents are re-queued, a dependent that already acted externally is blocked for a person, because a changed input never repeats an outside action by itself. External steps carry an operation key (`wf:<run>:<step>:<iteration>`); the proposing tool uses it as the proposal's idempotency key and the task records the proposal reference the moment it exists, so a crash after proposing and a retry after it both find the reference and wait on the proposal instead of acting again. The run acts as ADX's job identity at marketer level, so nothing it proposes is self-approved; a proposal denied by policy fails the step with the policy's reason and nothing reaches the outbox. Tools are the skill's permitted tools only; a call outside them is refused before dispatch. Loops repeat while the output asks and the bound allows; the bound is the definition's. Token budgets block a run before it spends more. The model runner offers the permitted tools, forces a structured completion that must fit the skill's output schema, and treats tool results as data.

- **Why.** The gates: a restart does not repeat a completed external action, a dependency version change invalidates the affected downstream result, cycles and unbounded generation are rejected, no tool call bypasses policy.
- **Cost.** Dispatch is a 30-second periodic tick rather than a River job per task; River still carries the run kinds that existed, and a tick is idempotent. With no model configured the runner is absent and ready tasks hold with the reason. Read tools available to workflows are the four Ask ADX reads; domain reads named in the catalogue are not wired yet and a step calling one is told so.

### BD-51. One supervisor inbox over every domain, autonomy by capability with recommend as the default, arbitration by configured precedence or by a person, and a kill switch that every entry point obeys
2026-10-17. The inbox gathers what waits on a person from each domain: proposals awaiting approval, held, uncertain and failed execution intents, blocked and failed workflow steps, failed runs, pending call readings, unknown calls, CRM field conflicts, open match candidates, escalated recommendation conflicts, engaged kill switches and a missing write policy; each item names the actions its domain accepts, and acting runs that domain's own function with the person's own permissions, so the supervisor adds no authority. The autonomy configuration is versioned: objective precedence in order, and per capability a mode (recommend, approval required, allowed) with a daily cap. An agent's proposal asks the supervisor first: with no configuration, or under recommend or approval-required, the proposal waits for a person even when policy would let the role act alone (the proposals service carries a require-approval flag for this); the cap refuses the day's excess; every recommendation is recorded with its source and objective. Arbitration finds live recommendations whose amounts exceed an envelope's remaining budget: with precedence covering all their objectives it keeps the higher ones while they fit and rejects the rest, recording the conflict as arbitrated; otherwise it escalates and touches nothing, and a person keeps one. The atomic reservation at execution still refuses the second of two approved proposals that would overdraw an envelope. A proposal denied under one policy stays denied after the policy changes: approval and execution refuse it, and the way forward is a new proposal that names the old one and is evaluated under today's policy. The kill switch is policy's: proposals are denied, messaging sends and CRM field dispatches are held, the workflow engine leases nothing, and calls are blocked while it is engaged.

- **Why.** The gates: conflicting agent recommendations cannot both consume the same allocation, a missing precedence routes the conflict to an operator, changing policy cannot retroactively authorize a prior forbidden action, the account kill switch applies to every entry point.
- **Cost.** Arbitration by a job actor records what it would reject and leaves the rejection to an admin's action, because a rejection is a decision with an identity. Objectives are free text until Reportage names them; nothing maps a proposal to an objective except the agent that made it.

### BD-52. Memory keeps advice, decision, action and delayed outcome apart; outcomes attach to the intervention whose window covers them; insights climb only on observed outcomes and a controlled comparison, and a model's agreement counts for nothing
2026-10-17. A learning record is opened once per recommendation with its source and subject; a person decides it adopted, modified (both naming the action that followed and when) or ignored (no action, ever). Outcomes are observed later with a metric, a value, a class (observed, attributed, control) and the observation time; an outcome attaches to the most recent adopted or modified record on the same subject whose action window covers it, so an improvement lands on the intervention that preceded it, never on advice nobody took, and an outcome no window covers stays unattached and is counted. Insights are statements in a lineage of immutable versions. A model's statement is marked as the model's; support items of kind "model agreement" are kept on the record and never counted. A hypothesis becomes supported with at least three supporting records (adopted or modified, with an observed outcome; attributed outcomes do not qualify), and a supported insight becomes validated only with evidence of an observed controlled comparison; only then is it causal. The model's actor can propose but never promote. A revision is a new version in the lineage, starts as a hypothesis and retires the old version. Memory feeds validated and supported findings, with lineage and version, into plan generation context and comparative research reports; hypotheses are never fed forward.

- **Why.** The gates: model agreement is not factual validation, a delayed outcome attaches to the correct cohort, ignored advice is not counted as an executed intervention, an attributed improvement is not automatically causal lift.
- **Cost.** Records are opened by callers (the supervisor's recommendations, alerts, plans) rather than automatically for every proposal, so the history is as complete as the callers are. The controlled-comparison evidence is recognised by its kind containing "control"; the measurement domain's controlled checks produce it, and a hand-recorded holdout can too.
